Mike, saw VertexOne secure $131M in financing and acquire Accelerated Innovations to expand the utility CX platform.

Funding plus an acquisition usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before they cool, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for VertexOne off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress around 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Mike, quick follow-up for VertexOne.

After financing and an acquisition, expectations on pipeline climb faster than headcount can, and most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to hit the new number. The gap shows up late, and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings VertexOne needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Mike, last bit of proof for VertexOne.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how VertexOne's reply rate likely compares to peer utility-software vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Mike, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem. Timing matters right after financing and an acquisition, and I know integrating a new product line is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a utility-software motion? I will tailor it to VertexOne either way.
